title: Noun sentence - Double mubtada
description: The natural order M + K + MBK, the two allowed abnormal orders (مُقَدَّم and مُؤَخَّر), and the double Mubtada (M + M + K) that creates curiosity about the subject. Every example is a verbless noun sentence from the Quran with its reference.
source: Owner's lesson notes: Noun sentence lessons 1 to 3 (PDF) and Lesson 4, Double Mubtada

questions.text: In إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ (Al-Hijr 15:45), which component is not written in the ayah?
questions.explanation: إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ is the Mubtada and فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ is a Jaar Majroor, the Muta'allaq bil khabar. The Khabar is implied ("present"): "Surely the righteous are (present) in gardens and springs".

questions.text: What is the natural order of the 3 components of a noun sentence?
questions.explanation: The Mubtada comes first, then the Khabar, then the Muta'allaq bil khabar: M + K + MBK. A change in this order adds extra meaning to the sentence.

questions.text: A component that comes before its normal position is called:
questions.explanation: A component placed earlier than its place in M + K + MBK is مُقَدَّم (muqaddam). One placed later than its normal place is مُؤَخَّر (muakkhar).

questions.text: Which two abnormal orders are allowed in a noun sentence?

options.text: K (muqaddam) + M (muakkhar), and MBK + K + M
MBK (muqaddam) + M (muakkhar), and M + MBK (muqaddam) + K (muakkhar)
MBK (muqaddam) + K (muakkhar), and K + M + MBK
M + K + MBK, and K + MBK + M

questions.explanation: Only two abnormal orders are allowed: the Muta'allaq bil khabar moves before the Mubtada (MBK + M), or before the Khabar (M + MBK + K). In both, the MBK is the muqaddam.

questions.text: What is the order of the components in وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ (Al-Baqarah 2:95)?

options.text: M + K + MBK, the natural order

questions.explanation: اللَّهُ (M), then عَلِيمٌ (K), then بِالظَّالِمِينَ (MBK). Nothing has moved, so this is the natural order: "Allah is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers".

questions.text: What is the order of the components in هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (Al-Baqarah 2:39)?

options.text: M + K + MBK, the natural order

questions.explanation: هُمْ is the Mubtada. The Jaar Majroor فِيهَا comes before its normal place (muqaddam) and the Khabar خَالِدُونَ comes after its normal place (muakkhar): "They, in it, are abiding forever".

questions.text: In إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِالنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ (Al-Baqarah 2:143), which component is muqaddam?

options.text: None; it is in the natural order

questions.explanation: The Jaar Majroor بِالنَّاسِ comes before the Khabar لَرَءُوفٌ, so the order is M + MBK (muqaddam) + K (muakkhar). The Mubtada إِنَّ اللَّهَ is first, its normal place.

questions.text: In وَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمَصِيرُ (Al Imran 3:28), which component is muakkhar?

options.text: إِلَى اللَّهِ, the Muta'allaq bil khabar
None; it is in the natural order

questions.explanation: الْمَصِيرُ is the Mubtada, so its normal place is first. It comes after إِلَى اللَّهِ, so it is muakkhar and إِلَى اللَّهِ is muqaddam: "The return is ONLY to Allah".

questions.text: Which translation shows the exclusivity in لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِيَ دِينِ (Al-Kafirun 109:6)?

options.text: You have your religion, and I have mine.
ONLY your religion is for you, and ONLY my religion is for me.
Your religion is for you, and my religion is ONLY for me.
For you ONLY is your religion, and for me ONLY is my religion.

questions.explanation: In both halves the Jaar Majroor (لَكُمْ, لِيَ) comes before the Mubtada (دِينُكُمْ, دِينِ): MBK muqaddam + M muakkhar. ONLY goes before the muqaddam part each time.

questions.text: Which of these is in the natural order M + K + MBK?

options.text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ (Al Imran 3:119)

questions.explanation: In 3:119, إِنَّ اللَّهَ (M), عَلِيمٌ (K) and بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ (MBK) are in their normal places. In 6:59 and 2:115 the MBK is before the Mubtada, and in 2:282 بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ is before the Khabar.

questions.text: Which translation fits لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ (At-Taghabun 64:1)?

options.text: His is the dominion and the praise of others.
ONLY the dominion is His, and ONLY the praise is His.
The dominion belongs to Him, and the praise belongs to Him.
To Him ONLY belongs the dominion, and to Him ONLY belongs the praise.

questions.explanation: In both halves the Jaar Majroor لَهُ comes before the Mubtada (الْمُلْكُ, الْحَمْدُ): MBK muqaddam + M muakkhar. For exclusivity, ONLY goes before the muqaddam part, "to Him ONLY".

questions.text: What is a double Mubtada?

options.text: Two Mubtadas that come before the Khabar
A Mubtada that is repeated after the Khabar
Two Khabars that come after one Mubtada
A Mubtada that has a Muta'allaq bil khabar on both sides

questions.explanation: Sometimes two Mubtadas are used before the Khabar, giving the order M + M + K, as in وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ (Al-Baqarah 2:5).

questions.text: Why are two Mubtadas used before the Khabar?

options.text: To show that the Khabar is ONLY for the Mubtada
Because a pointing word can never be a Mubtada alone
To create interest or curiosity about the subject
To show that the sentence is a question

questions.explanation: The double Mubtada makes the listener wait for the Khabar, which creates interest or curiosity about the subject: "Those people, they are the successful ones". Exclusivity (ONLY) comes from a muqaddam component, not from a double Mubtada.

questions.text: What is the order of the components in وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ (Al-Baqarah 2:5)?
questions.explanation: أُولَٰئِكَ is the first Mubtada and هُمُ is the second; الْمُفْلِحُونَ is the Khabar: M + M + K, "Those people, they are the successful ones".

questions.text: In إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ (Al-Maidah 5:109), what are the two Mubtadas?
questions.explanation: إِنَّكَ, a harf of Nasb with its ism, is the first Mubtada, and أَنْتَ is the second. عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ, an إِضَافَة, is the Khabar: "Surely You, You are the Knower of the unseen".

questions.text: Which translation of إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ (Al-Baqarah 2:37) shows the double Mubtada?

options.text: Surely He, He is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.
Surely He is the One who accepts repentance, He is Merciful.
Surely the Accepter of repentance is He, the Merciful.
Surely He accepts repentance ONLY, the Merciful.

questions.explanation: إِنَّهُ is the first Mubtada and هُوَ the second, both before the Khabar التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ. The translation keeps both: "Surely He, He is...", which builds curiosity before the Khabar.

questions.text: Which translation of وَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ (Fatir 35:15) shows the double Mubtada?

options.text: And Allah is free of need of Him, the Praiseworthy.
And Allah, He is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
And ONLY to Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
And He is Allah, free of need and praiseworthy.

questions.explanation: اللَّهُ is the first Mubtada and هُوَ the second, so the Khabar الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ comes after both: M + M + K, "Allah, He is the Free of need".

questions.text: Which of these has a double Mubtada?
questions.explanation: In 2:27, أُولَٰئِكَ and هُمُ are two Mubtadas before the Khabar الْخَاسِرُونَ (M + M + K). 2:39 is M + MBK + K, 45:36 is MBK + M, and 2:95 is M + K + MBK, each with one Mubtada.

questions.text: Which translation of إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ (Adh-Dhariyat 51:58) shows the double Mubtada?

options.text: Surely Allah is ONLY the Provider.
Surely Allah, He is the Provider.
Surely the Provider of Allah is He.
Surely He is the Provider of Allah.

questions.explanation: إِنَّ اللَّهَ, a harf of Nasb with its ism, is the first Mubtada and هُوَ the second; الرَّزَّاقُ is the Khabar: M + M + K, "Surely Allah, He is the Provider".

questions.text: In إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ (Al-Isra 17:1), which word is the second Mubtada?
questions.explanation: إِنَّهُ is the first Mubtada and هُوَ is the second. السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ is the Khabar that comes after them: "Surely He, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing".
